source.title: Augment the Cache, Replace the Activation: A 2x2 Study of Internal-State Sharing
source.authors: Adam Deng; Shi-Cheng Liu; Ya-Da Zhu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether internal states can be consumed across models and refines the scope of interchangeability: transfer works in some same-family settings but fails across the tested model families.
record.gate_note: The study tests behavioral transfer of shared internal states, not convergence of representations with model scale or capability. It reports representational-fidelity measures such as cosine alongside transfer results; these are included where they directly describe tested cross-model compatibility. Cited results from other papers are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The distinct-checkpoint and cross-family experiments test V4 by measuring whether foreign internal states support the receiver's answers. Most other experiments use identical holder and receiver weights and test content transport within one model, rather than interchangeability between models.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that KV augmentation and correctly aligned activation replacement work in their controlled fact-transfer task, with the positive mechanism comparisons primarily using identical holder and receiver weights. A receiver-trained bridge also serves one very close held-out checkpoint, but fails on the coder and math checkpoints and every tested cross-family configuration. Activation replacement requires oracle position and layer alignment; native-reference ties do not establish superiority.
record.recipe_differences: Measures downstream behavioral transfer after sharing internal states, rather than representational similarity or convergence with scale. Uses cache augmentation, activation replacement, and cross-model compatibility probes.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer changes with carrier and mechanism, the activation injection layer, sender/cache similarity, and whether the sender is cross-family. The paper also reports different results across cache adaptation settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Same-model keys selected or synthesized at high geometric fidelity fail to preserve answers, while exact self-keys reproduce the native ceiling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric similarity to a model's own keys does not guarantee behavioral substitutability of those keys.

fits_no_version.finding: For identical holder and receiver weights, KV augmentation transfers content, and correctly positioned activation replacement approaches native performance more closely than activation augmentation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one frozen model, internal content transfer depends on the carrier, consumption mechanism, and injection alignment.

record.problems: The results concern a controlled latent fact-transfer task rather than general representational convergence. Most positive results use one model family; cross-family results collapse. Activation replacement is given oracle position and layer alignment. Every run uses a single seed. The cache holder contains the answer passage verbatim, and the paper notes copying is not fully eliminated. The interpolation table's alpha=0 values appear inconsistent with the separately described identity arm.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted the multi-source pool-size results in Appendix A.1, the architecture sweep of substitution in Appendix A.3, additional activation replacement controls and mismatch-control values in Table 3, the activation-side cross-family trained-router individual cells in Appendix A.6, and the reported geometric tolerance/readout-gain measurements in Appendix A.5. These were not expanded into separate rows; some are described in R54 or the problems field. The extracted rows prioritize the detailed substitution grid, adaptation ladder, replacement depths, and held-out sender outcomes.

untested.parts: No relationship between model scale or capability and cross-model representational alignment is measured. The architecture sweep probes each receiver separately.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
No independently initialized networks are compared for shared features or subspaces.

No general test of pairwise optimal linear maps, relative representations, unpaired alignment, or cross-model layer stitching. Cross-family failure concerns the tested intermediate-state interfaces and alignment methods; it does not establish failure of all simple maps.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.
No test that measured representational convergence changes with similarity metrics, metric settings, or input distribution. Neighbour rank here controls key substitution, not a convergence metric.
No convergence plateau or causal comparison of shared data/objectives against a common model of reality.

missing.what: Separate raw-attention outcomes for distinct held-out senders: instruct shared accuracy 0.145, below floor but with control-subtracted lift +0.070; coder and math raw lifts both 0.000. The instruct result appears only in R55's note, and the other raw outcomes have no rows.

record.verdict_notes: The main extraction error is treating same-weight content transport as cross-model interchangeability. Those experiments remain useful controls and related findings. Table 1's alpha=0 values conflict with the separately reported identity result and should not be reconciled by assumption. Declared omissions need not be re-listed as missing. Behavioral transfer runs use one seed; the conditioning measurement separately reports three seeds.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep measuring representational convergence.
No paired image-caption or vision-language representation comparison.
No comparison of independently initialized seeds of the same architecture for shared features or subspaces.
Tests behavioral consumption of internal states and some cross-model compatibility, but not linear representation maps, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment as such.
No recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.

Does not systematically test convergence across similarity measures, neighbor settings, or input distributions. Its fidelity-versus-consumability results do not establish the stated metric/data dependence of convergence.
Does not test whether shared data or objectives cause convergence rather than a common model of reality.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Same-family sharing and closely matched held-out sender
reader_labels.reason: Cache augmentation transfers above floor for same-model states (R40–R43), activation replacement reaches the native reference in the tested aligned setting (R48–R52), and the nearest held-out sender has positive control-subtracted lift (R55).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.label: challenges
